findings.title: Blocked-continuation history is presented without freshness
findings.what: The detector retains each contributing session's latestTimestamp, but lines 76-104 emit an undated present-tense recommendation and provenance with no asOf/stale fields. Old retained stop-hook events therefore look current.
findings.fix: Derive the newest plausible contributing timestamp, attach provenance.asOf/stale, use "As of <date>" for stale history, and prepend a re-check action when stale.
findings.acceptance: A fixture containing only sufficiently old blocked events emits provenance.asOf with stale=true, dated detail beginning "As of <date>", and a re-check action; fresh events remain dated but not stale.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed latestTimestamp is computed at lines 42 and 47-48 but is used only for sorting; the returned recommendation at lines 76-104 never exposes or evaluates freshness.

findings.title: Unused-rule detector can encourage removal of safety-relevant bare-tool denies
findings.what: Only Bash rules with specifiers pass through isDangerousDenyRule. A bare-tool rule such as Write, Edit, WebFetch, or another privileged tool reaches the unused list solely because no retained call matched, after which lines 53-61 describe it as non-destructive clutter and recommend pruning it.
findings.fix: Restrict pruning advice to an explicit allowlist of demonstrably low-risk rules, or classify every supported bare tool for safety and suppress removal advice for privileged or unknown tools.
findings.acceptance: Tests with unused bare-tool denies for privileged and unknown tools produce no prune recommendation, while an explicitly classified low-risk unused rule can still be reported.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read lines 24-43: bare-tool rules have specifier=null, bypass the Bash dangerous-rule check, and are appended whenever retained toolData has no match. No other safety classification exists in this file.

findings.title: Validated prune snippet performs the opposite configuration change
findings.what: The label and note say to remove unused deny entries, but the emitted JSON snippet is {permissions:{deny:unused}}. Because fixKind is omitted, repository fix semantics treat it as a copy-paste validated fix; merging it preserves or adds the rules rather than pruning them. The recommendation also lacks structured provenance for its retained-history claim.
findings.fix: Do not emit an additive JSON snippet for deletion. Mark the fix manual with explicit removal instructions (or use a supported deletion patch format), and add observations citing liveConfig.settings.permissions.deny plus toolData match coverage and freshness.
findings.acceptance: The recommendation's effective fix kind is manual unless a deletion-safe format exists; applying the displayed operation removes only the cited entries, and provenance validation passes with retained-history scope and date represented.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the contradiction at lines 60-62. Directly related baseline fix-validity semantics state an absent fixKind defaults to validated, so this is not merely wording or style.

findings.title: Backup policy state is called current without an observation date
findings.what: The detector correctly selects the latest retained transition per dimension, but lines 89-106 call it a current risk-increasing change without exposing the newest backup timestamp, asOf, or stale status. A years-old final transition is indistinguishable from current posture.
findings.fix: Derive freshness from the newest contributing DriftEvent.timestamp, attach structured asOf/stale provenance, and change stale detail to "As of <date>" with an action to verify live policy.
findings.acceptance: Old drift fixtures emit dated stale wording, provenance.asOf and stale=true, and a verify-current-policy action; recent drift is dated and stale=false.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed timestamps are used at lines 48 and 55 only for state selection and ordering; the emitted detail and provenance at lines 85-107 contain no date or freshness qualification.

findings.title: Prompt-friction fix grants unrestricted access to arbitrary non-Bash tools
findings.what: When the dominant prompt-prone tool is not Bash, allowRules becomes [top.toolName] and the snippet places that bare tool in permissions.allow. The evidence establishes frequency only, not safe variants, so tools capable of writes, network access, or other privileged actions can be blanket-authorized.
findings.fix: Generate fixes only for an explicit catalog of scoped, reviewed safe rules. For unknown or privileged tools, emit manual analysis with no allow snippet; never equate prompt frequency with authorization safety.
findings.acceptance: A dominant privileged non-Bash tool produces no permissions.allow snippet, while catalogued safe scoped operations can produce a validated rule; tests cover Write/Edit/network-capable and unknown tool names.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 18-19 choose the bare tool name for every non-Bash value and lines 45-48 serialize it directly into allow; there is no safety allowlist or operation-level evidence in this file.

findings.title: Prompt-friction safety claim lacks provenance and validated evidence
findings.what: The output claims to allowlist safe variants, but the only evidence is aggregate tool frequency. It emits no structured provenance, and omitting fixKind makes the broad snippet validated by default despite no artifact showing which non-Bash operations were safe.
findings.fix: Add structured observations for promptable call count, denominator/share, sessions, and exact safe-rule derivation; mark unproven recommendations manual and omit their snippets.
findings.acceptance: Provenance validation passes, percentage arithmetic is tied to cited numerator and denominator fields, and no fix is effectively validated unless every emitted rule is derived from reviewed operation-level evidence.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed lines 26-32 expose only aggregate counts and lines 34-50 emit a fix with neither provenance nor fixKind. Frequency cannot reproduce the claimed safe-operation scope.

findings.title: Risky-action history is emitted without as-of or stale demotion
findings.what: The detector reports historical tool calls in present-tense review language and provenance but never derives freshness. RiskyAction evidence references can carry timestamps, yet lines 91-114 provide no asOf/stale qualification.
findings.fix: Use contributing action or evidenceRef timestamps to derive the newest plausible date, add provenance.asOf/stale, and use "As of <date>" plus a re-check instruction for stale history; remain explicitly undated when timestamp coverage is incomplete.
findings.acceptance: Old action fixtures emit stale=true and dated wording; fresh complete fixtures emit stale=false with asOf; malformed or incomplete timestamp coverage does not fabricate a date.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed evidenceRefs are collected at lines 78-80 and tests demonstrate they include timestamps, but the returned provenance at lines 103-114 records only a count and inference.
